item.subject: maths
item.stem:
The diagram shows quadrilateral ABCD. Anvi measures $\angle A = \angle B = \angle C = \angle D = 90^\circ$.

Can she classify ABCD as a rectangle without separately checking that opposite sides are equal?

options.A: Yes: a quadrilateral with all angles $90^\circ$ is a rectangle; opposite-side equalities then follow.
options.B: She should call the figure a right angle, not a rectangle.
options.C: Yes, even if A, B, C, D were only three rays and not a closed quadrilateral.
options.D: The same rule also classifies any open broken line of four right turns as a rectangle.
